info.description: Identity and authorization in one system. Enforcer signs users in, holds who they are (tenants, roles, groups), and answers whether an actor may perform an action on a resource, returning the decision, the policy that made it, and the reason. Because the caller is resolved before evaluation, a policy is handed a real accessor object rather than a bare subject id.

All query filters intersect (AND). since/until run on accounts.created_at and are parsed by the same window parser /accounts/summary uses, so the formats and error codes cannot drift between the two endpoints. post.description: Sets active=true on every id in the body, applying the SAME per-target authorization (ResourceAuth manage, so a tenant_admin can only touch accounts in their own tenant) and the same admin-role-escalation fence as the single-account PUT /accounts/{id}/active. Never all-or-nothing: each id is authorized and applied independently, and the response reports succeeded/failed counts plus a per-id ok|forbidden|error result rather than aborting the batch on the first failure.

Sets active=false on every id in the body — the deactivation twin of bulkActivateAccounts, with the identical per-target authorization, escalation fence, and partial-failure reporting (succeeded/failed counts plus a per-id ok|forbidden|error result). Deactivating does not touch sessions or API keys; combine with bulkInvalidateAccountSessions to force those accounts out immediately.

IRREVERSIBLE. Purges every id in the body via the same transactional full purge as DELETE /accounts/{id} (each id its own transaction; see docs/data-retention.md) — not a bulk deactivation. Per-target ResourceAuth manage is enforced independently for each id (a tenant_admin can only delete within their own tenant); the response reports succeeded/failed counts and a per-id ok|forbidden|error result, so a partially-authorized batch still deletes everything it was allowed to.

Resolves many email addresses to account ids within ONE tenant, case-insensitively, in a single query — the read an importer runs BEFORE it writes anything, so the operator can see and fix unmatched rows while nothing has happened yet. Read-only and idempotent. Every input line comes back with a verdict in the order it was sent, with the email echoed exactly as supplied so a caller can line the answer up against its own file: `found` (with account_id and active) or `not_found`. An account that exists but is inactive is still `found` — whether that disqualifies it is the caller's policy. An email belonging to ANOTHER tenant comes back not_found, exactly like one that exists nowhere: the tenant is the whole boundary. Cross-tenant callers MUST pass tenant_id; tenant-scoped callers may pass their own or omit it. At most 1000 emails per call.

get.description: Typo-tolerant identity search over username, first/last name, email and phone, ranked by pg_trgm trigram similarity. Matches when EITHER the similarity operator fires (typo tolerance, governed by pg_trgm.similarity_threshold) OR q is a plain substring of the haystack OR q exactly equals the account's Privy DID. Row visibility is the identical compiled authz filter GET /accounts uses, so this endpoint cannot surface anything the plain list would hide. Like every tenant-bearing list, the search covers the caller's OWN session tenant unless it says otherwise — platform admins included. tenant_id=<another tenant> and all_tenants=true require the cross_tenant grant (403 otherwise); passing both, or a malformed value, is a 400. scoped_to_tenant names the tenant searched (empty with all_tenants=true, which also sets all_tenants). Service accounts are excluded by default; kind=service|all surfaces them for tenant admins.

get.description: One account by id (ResourceAuth read — visible to the account itself, its tenant admins, and platform admins). 404 account_not_found for an unknown or out-of-scope id; the endpoint is not an existence oracle for ids outside the caller's authorized scope.

delete.description: IRREVERSIBLE full purge (ResourceAuth manage — admin or tenant_admin only). In ONE transaction it hard-deletes the account and everything keyed to it — sessions, API keys, identity links, wallets, contacts held by and pointing at it, verification sessions, terms acceptances, tickets it raised and messages it wrote, invites, sign-in telemetry, PIN — and, when no other live membership uses the person, the person row with its devices and verifications. Money records (fulfillments, settlements) and the audit log are kept; they reference ids only. Then best-effort removes the upstream Privy user. An account still referenced by agent history is kept as a PII-free tombstone instead of deleted. 409 has_agent when the account is the service account of a live agent. See docs/data-retention.md. For a reversible block use PUT /accounts/{id}/active with active=false instead.

patch.description: Partial update of an account's profile fields; absent fields are unchanged. Behind a write-level resource check (the account itself, its tenant's admin, or a platform admin); a caller outside the account's tenant gets 404, as for an id that does not exist. timezone is the account's own display zone, an IANA name such as America/Chicago checked against the platform zone database (400 invalid_timezone); null or "" clears it, meaning "use the workspace zone". timezone is SELF-ONLY: a body carrying it for any account but the caller's own is 403 self_only and nothing in the body is written, whatever the caller's role.

put.description: Flips one account's active flag (ResourceAuth manage). The reversible counterpart to DELETE /accounts/{id}: setting active=false blocks the account without removing data, upstream identity, or history. Returns 403 forbidden if the caller would be escalating an admin account's access, the same fence bulkActivateAccounts/bulkDeactivateAccounts enforce per-target.

get.summary: Passkey MFA status for an account

get.description: Twilio Lookup v2 risk for an account's phone. Self for any authed user; tenant_admin/admin/developer for any account.

delete.description: Removed: no role — including admin and tenant_admin — sets, changes, clears or reads another account's PIN. A locked-out user recovers through the verified-contact reset (/auth/me/pin/reset/start). The route keeps its ActionManage gate (callers without it still get 403/404 exactly as before, so nothing new is disclosed) and then answers 410 `pin_admin_reset_removed` without touching the PIN.

put.description: Assigns a role slug to one account (ResourceAuth manage). Rejects with 403 forbidden if the change would escalate an account to admin beyond what the caller may grant, and with 400 unknown_role if the slug does not exist as a role in scope. Role changes take effect immediately — role is read fresh from the account row on every request, never trusted from an old JWT claim.

get.description: Auth-funnel events for one tenant, newest first — including the attempts that never reached an account, which is the whole point. Pass email to answer "did this address ever try, and what failed": the address is hashed server-side and matched against the stored hash, so the search term is never written to the database and the plaintext never had to be stored to be findable. Scoped to the caller's tenant; only a cross-tenant admin may name another via tenant_id. from/to accept RFC3339 or YYYY-MM-DD. Unknown query parameters are a 400, not a silently unfiltered list.

get.description: The email dead-letter queue: messages that failed delivery and were parked rather than lost, newest first by default. Optional topic filter is a case-insensitive substring match on the wire topic. from/to bound created_at (when the message was parked) so a retry sweep can be scoped to a window: YYYY-MM-DD is an inclusive whole UTC day, RFC3339 an exact instant (from inclusive, to exclusive); malformed is 400 invalid_from / invalid_to. total counts the entries matching every filter. There is no status filter: the queue has no status — an entry is parked until replayed or dropped, and either removes it. Pair with replayEmailDlqEntry to resend one or deleteEmailDlqEntry to drop it.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: created_at lower bound (inclusive): YYYY-MM-DD or RFC3339

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: created_at upper bound: YYYY-MM-DD (inclusive day) or RFC3339 (exclusive)

parameters.name: sort_dir
parameters.description: sort direction (id breaks ties in the same direction)

get.description: The CS failed-P2P dashboard: fulfillments across the tenant. Party scope is OPTIONAL: `user_id` matches EITHER side (sender, receiver or creator), while `sender_user_id` / `receiver_user_id` pin one end. All supplied filters intersect, so sender+receiver together mean "from A to B". Without them the list is tenant-wide and only pageable. `status` = closed (cancelled|declined|expired — the failed set), outstanding (pending|claimed|submitted), all, or an exact status. A system admin may pass ?tenant_id to view another tenant; tenant-scoped callers (tenant_admin, developer) are pinned to their own. total matches the rows' filter.

parameters.name: user_id
parameters.description: scope to one person on EITHER side (sender, receiver or creator)

parameters.name: sender_user_id
parameters.description: scope to transfers SENT by this user

parameters.name: receiver_user_id
parameters.description: scope to transfers RECEIVED by this user

parameters.name: reference_prefix
parameters.description: reference starts with this literal prefix (e.g. RWD:<group_id>:) — payout-campaign rows

parameters.name: group_id
parameters.description: sugar for reference_prefix=RWD:<group_id>: — everything fanned out from this payout group

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: p2p (no machine tag — a real person-to-person transfer) | deposit (DEPOSIT:) | billpay (BP:) | direct (DIRECT:) | reward (RWD:) | terminal (TERMINAL: — a POS sale)

parameters.name: self_payments
parameters.description: include (default) | exclude | only — sender == receiver rows (bill-pay funding, quick pays, self-sends)

parameters.name: tx_hash
parameters.description: exact on-chain hash (case-insensitive) — what a customer pastes into a ticket

parameters.name: customer_guid
parameters.description: scope to a CYBRID customer guid, resolved to the account(s) holding it (other providers write their own id shapes into the same column and are not searched); a guid belonging to nobody returns an EMPTY page, never the tenant

parameters.name: overpaid
parameters.description: only | exclude — rows whose summed ROUTED settlements EXCEED notional_uoa. A memo is a payer-supplied bytes32 that can be routed more than once, and a route may declare a larger notional than the request asked for; either way the receiver holds more than the record says was owed.

get.description: Bucketed counts + notional sums for a single user, for the operator activity chart. `user_id` is matched on EITHER side (sender, receiver or creator) — the same party test GET /admin/fulfillments uses, so the chart and the list it drills into agree about whose transfer a row is. `bucket` is day|week|month. Sent/received split by the CHARTED user's role, not the caller's. `settled` counts only confirmed; `cancelled` folds cancelled|declined|expired and is returned as its OWN series rather than dropped — climbing cancellations are signal. `self_payments` defaults to **exclude**: a self→self fulfillment is funding plumbing, and counting it as customer activity misreads treasury operations as behaviour. Aggregated in SQL, so cost scales with buckets rather than transfers.
get.summary: One person's P2P activity over time (admin)

get.description: Operator point lookup for a transfer named in a ticket. Fenced to the caller's tenant (or `tenant_id` for the admin role): an id in another tenant is a 404, never a 403, so the endpoint is not an existence oracle. Counterparty contact PII is scrubbed — the operator is not a party.

System admin, or a role carrying the `mpp_ops` grant. Oldest first. `forwarder` finds the intent behind a deposit address (an exact match; a malformed address is 400 invalid_filter). Each row is the intent, its fulfillment's status and every transfer seen at its forwarder. `state=received,overpaid` is what an operator settles; `underpaid,parked` (and expired) is what an operator refunds. Read-only.
get.summary: List MPP deposit intents (system admin or mpp_ops): the manual-settle queue

parameters.name: forwarder
parameters.description: exact deposit (forwarder) address, 0x + 40 hex, any case

post.description: The settle worker's second step after mode=reserve: stores the hashes on the (intent, kind) reservation and moves the intent (settle -> settling, refund -> refunded). Sends nothing. 409 action_already_completed when the reservation already has a tx hash; 409 no_reservation when there is none.
post.summary: Record the tx hashes sent for a reserved settle/refund (system admin)

post.description: Returns the exact call (forwarder refund, after a factory deploy if needed) without sending anything unless dry_run is explicitly false. Refused unless the intent is underpaid, overpaid, parked or expired. Idempotent per intent. mode=reserve reserves the intent and returns the plan with action_id. A non-dry refund answers 409 refund_to_contract when the refund address has code or is a forwarder.
post.summary: Refund an MPP deposit intent (system admin, dry_run by default)

post.description: Drops the (intent, kind) reservation only while it has no tx hash, so the lever can be taken again. 409 action_already_completed when the row records a sent transaction; 409 no_reservation when there is none.
post.summary: Release a reserved settle/refund that sent nothing (system admin)

post.description: Returns the exact calls (factory deploy if needed, then forwarder settle) without sending anything unless dry_run is explicitly false. Refused unless the intent is received or overpaid. Idempotent per intent: a repeat returns the first result. mode=reserve (the settle worker) reserves the intent before anything is sent and returns the plan with action_id and reserved=true; the worker then calls .../complete with the hashes or .../release. max_input_amount (> 0) replaces the quoted max input.
post.summary: Settle an MPP deposit intent (system admin, dry_run by default)

get.description: System admin, or a role carrying the `mpp_ops` grant. A read-only alias of POST /admin/mpp-deposit-intents/{id}/settle with dry_run (the same builder, default fee and deadline knobs): the exact calls a signer would send ({to, data, value, description}: factory deploy when the forwarder has no code, then the forwarder's settle), the amounts, the receiver and refund address, the forwarder's live MPP balance (`on_chain_balance`, null when it could not be read), the fulfillment status, and a verdict. Nothing is reserved, sent or changed. `steps` is empty unless `settleable`. `reason` when not settleable: already_confirmed (fulfillment confirmed or intent settling/settled), already_refunded, expired (settle reverts after expiry), underfunded (holds less MPP than quoted_max_input), wrong_token (parked: a non-MPP token arrived and too little MPP is held), not_received (funded, but the intent is not received/overpaid, so the settle lever would refuse).
get.summary: Read an MPP deposit intent's settle plan (system admin or mpp_ops, read-only)

This is how you find every account one human holds across tenants and spot a duplicate signup; an account-level search cannot see across tenant boundaries. tenant_id restricts to persons with a live account in that tenant; invited_by restricts to persons with an account invited by a given account id.

parameters.description: restrict to persons with a live account in this tenant

parameters.name: invited_by
parameters.description: restrict to persons with an account invited by this account id

parameters.name: group_id
parameters.description: restrict to persons holding a live account that is a member of this group; 404 group_not_found if the group is not visible to you

parameters.name: exclude_group_id
parameters.description: drop persons holding a live account in this group; 404 group_not_found if not visible

get.description: One person's platform-wide record: identity fields and every account they hold, across every tenant. Requires the cross-tenant grant, same as listPersons.

delete.description: Cascading soft-delete of a cross-tenant PERSON, not a single account. A tenant_admin caller only removes that person's membership in the ADMIN'S OWN tenant — other tenants' accounts for the same person survive untouched; a system-admin (cross_tenant) caller deletes the person platform-wide. reason is optional and recorded for audit.

patch.description: Partial PII patch on a cross-tenant person: a field present in the JSON body is applied — even an empty string clears it — while an absent field is left unchanged, so a {} body is a no-op. username is rejected with 400 (it is account-scoped, not person-scoped; use PATCH /accounts/{id} instead). The regulated block — DOB, home address, primary email and phone — is echoed back in the response only to a system-admin (global) caller, never to a tenant_admin, so an empty patch cannot be used as a read of those fields at the lower gate.

403.description: person_spans_tenants: a non-platform admin may only merge persons whose every membership is in their own tenant

409.description: merge_conflict, or service_account_involved if either person holds a service account
service_account_involved: the account is a service account

parameters.description: referrer username / email (substring) or account id (exact)

parameters.name: exclude_group_id
parameters.description: drop referrers who are members of this group; 404 group_not_found if not visible

get.description: Every role in the catalog, built-in and custom — roles are a global table with no tenant_id, so this is not tenant-scoped. Gated on tenant_read or above; see also listRoles (GET /roles), the same underlying data exposed to ANY authenticated caller with no admin gate, for populating a role picker. total counts the roles matching q; an unknown sort falls back to slug.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: case-insensitive substring of slug, name or description

parameters.name: sort_dir
parameters.description: sort direction (id breaks ties in the same direction)

post.description: Creates a custom role with an arbitrary permission grant. System-admin (platform-only) gated — there is no separate escalation fence because only a caller who already holds cross_tenant (the maximum grant) can reach this route at all. slug must match ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{1,49}$ (mixed case is lowercased, not rejected) and may not collide with a built-in slug (admin, tenant_admin, developer, user), which returns 409.

get.description: One role by id, including its full permission grant (cross_tenant, tenant_read, tenant_write, tenant_manage, admin_managed).

post.description: Mints a new API key for the CALLER's own account and returns the plaintext exactly once in this response — it is never retrievable again. name is required and cannot be blank: an unnamed key is a working credential nobody can identify to revoke later, so an empty or whitespace-only name is rejected with 400 missing_fields rather than silently minting an anonymous key. scope is optional and space-delimited, in the same vocabulary OAuth grants (enforcer:read | enforcer:write | enforcer:admin | policy:self | enforcer:<tag>.<effect>); the key stores it and the response echoes it. A key never exceeds its owner's role and permissions, and a scope narrows it further. A caller whose own credential carries a scope may only mint at or below it (the coarse ladder read < write < admin; a fine scope is covered by its own tag at an equal-or-wider effect or by a covering coarse scope) and is refused with 403 insufficient_scope otherwise; such a caller that omits scope gets a key carrying its own scope, never an unscoped one. An unscoped caller (a login session, an unscoped API key) may mint any scope or none. An unknown scope is 400 invalid_scope. expires_at is optional, RFC 3339, and must be in the future (400 invalid_expires_at otherwise); once it passes the key is refused with 401 on both the HTTP X-API-Key path and the gRPC transport, exactly like a revoked key. Omitted, the key never expires. The response records created_by, the account that minted the key. A caller presenting an agent (ag_, or an agent client_credentials token) or portal-link credential may never mint a key: 403 agent_cannot_mint (AGENTS_CONTRACT §5.3).

post.description: Enrolls a 4- or 6-digit PIN for the CALLER (self only, every role). First enrollment only and atomic: of concurrent enrollments exactly one persists, the others get 409 `pin_already_set` (changes go through the 2FA reset flow). 412 `no_verified_contact` when the account has no verified email or phone on file. 403 `person_credential_required` for API keys, portal links, agent and OAuth/delegated tokens — only the person's own sign-in manages a PIN. 429 `rate_limited` (Retry-After header and `data.retry_after`, same seconds) past 5 per account / 20 per IP per 15 minutes. The PIN is stored only as a salted argon2id digest and never returned or logged.

Completes the CALLER's self-service reset: the code from /auth/me/pin/reset/start plus the new 4- or 6-digit PIN (+ `channel`, optional; when sent it must match the channel the code went to). The code is bound to this account, its channel and the verified destination; it is single-use, valid 10 minutes and voided after 5 wrong tries. Consuming the code and installing the PIN are one transaction: any refusal leaves the old PIN working. Refusals, all 401: `reset_code_invalid` (wrong code), `reset_code_expired` (expired, never requested, or the verified destination changed), `reset_code_used` (already spent), `reset_code_attempts_exceeded` (5 wrong codes), `reset_channel_mismatch`, `reset_retry_start` (SMS only: the code was right and the provider spent it, but the PIN write lost a race with a resend, expiry or another completion; the old PIN still works, request a new code). Installing the new PIN also clears any lockout. 403 `person_credential_required` for delegated credentials. 429 `rate_limited` (Retry-After header and `data.retry_after`) past 10 per account / 30 per IP per 15 minutes.

requestBody.description: code + new pin (+ channel when it was chosen explicitly)

post.description: Sends a 6-digit one-time code to the CALLER's verified contact: `channel` "email" or "sms", or omit to auto-pick (email when verified, else SMS). The response discloses only the channel, a masked destination, `code_length` (6) and `expires_at` (10 minutes). Every start REPLACES the previous code on both channels (SMS: Twilio Verify may re-deliver the same digits while its own verification is pending; the server-side ticket is still replaced). 412 `no_verified_contact` when nothing verified is on file; 400 `channel_unavailable` when the requested channel has no verified destination. 403 `person_credential_required` for delegated credentials. 429 `rate_limited` (Retry-After header and `data.retry_after`) past 3 per account / 10 per IP per 15 minutes. There is no administrative PIN reset.

Checks the CALLER's entered PIN. Proves check-in identity only: it never issues a session, token or scope. A wrong PIN is 401 `pin_incorrect` with `data.attempts_remaining`; the 5th consecutive wrong PIN — and any entry while locked, even the right PIN — is 423 `pin_locked` with `data.locked_until`, a Retry-After header and `data.retry_after` (the same seconds, for clients that keep only the body). The lock lasts 15 minutes, is shared with every kiosk and replica, and touches no session or role. 404 `pin_not_set` when no PIN is enrolled. 403 `person_credential_required` for delegated credentials. 429 `rate_limited` (Retry-After header and `data.retry_after`) past 10 per account / 30 per IP per 15 minutes.

get.description: The onboarding gate: the caller's current terms per type (a tenant-specific version overrides the global one for the same type), each flagged accepted/accepted_at, plus has_mandatory_pending — true if any MANDATORY document among them is still unaccepted. Poll this after acceptMyTerms to confirm the gate cleared.

delete.description: Withdraws the caller's own consent to a document by id (idempotent — revoking an unaccepted or already-revoked id is a no-op). The acceptance row is deleted, but the revocation itself is retained in the audit log for compliance. Revoking a MANDATORY document's acceptance will re-trip has_mandatory_pending on the next getMyTerms call.

post.description: Records the caller's consent to one document by id, snapshotting its content hash, version, IP and user-agent at accept time — so a later edit to the document's content never retroactively changes what the caller is considered to have agreed to. Idempotent: re-accepting an already-accepted id is a no-op, not a duplicate row or an error.

Public: starts the native `email_otp` login/registration flow by emailing a one-time code to `email` (optionally scoped by `tenant_code`). Always 200 `{message:"code sent"}` on success; the code itself is only echoed in the response body when the deployment has `expose_dev_otp` enabled (local/dev only). An expired workspace code gets 404 `tenant_code_expired`. Send the Cloudflare Turnstile widget response as `turnstile_token`: when the deployment has Turnstile configured, a sent token that fails is 403 `turnstile_failed` (503 `turnstile_unavailable` if Cloudflare cannot be reached), and a deployment with `otp_require_turnstile` on refuses a missing one the same way. 429 `rate_limited` when the caller's address or the email's send budget (per address, across workspaces: by default 5 codes per 10 minutes and 20 per hour) is spent.

parameters.name: X-Email-Brand
parameters.description: Optional look of the code email. `gvnr` sends the GVNR-branded mail; any other value, or none, sends the default. It changes nothing but the email's look.

post.description: Mints a single-use, 60-second hand-off for the signed-in person and returns the travel site's SSO URL carrying it. The token is opaque and is NOT a credential for this API. Refused with 403 `email_unverified` when the account has no verified email (the travel site keys accounts by email), 404 `partner_sso_unavailable` when the tenant is not enabled, 400 `invalid_navigate_to` for anything but a path on the travel site, 400 `unknown_launch_host` when `launch_host` names no configured travel site (empty = the default site), and 403 `person_session_required` for delegated credentials.

Called by the Xeni travel platform, not by apps. Body is `{"jwtToken": "<hand-off>"}`. Redeems the hand-off once and answers `{"status":true,"msg":"User token validated","data":{"first_name","last_name","email"}}`. Every failure — unknown, expired, already used, account disabled or unverified — is the same 403 `{"status":false,"msg":"Invalid token"}`.

get.description: The caller's own registered WebAuthn/passkey credentials — every one the signed-in PERSON holds, whichever of their workspaces it was added from; never anyone else's. Each carries `aaguid` and, when known, `provider` (the password manager or device that made it), plus `backup_eligible`/`backup_state` (a synced passkey has both).

delete.description: Removes one of the signed-in person's passkeys. Refused with 403 `reauth_required` unless this session signed in within the last 15 minutes (sign in again, then retry), and with 409 `last_sign_in_method` when it is the person's last passkey and the account has no verified email to fall back on. 403 `person_credential_required` for API keys, portal links, agent and OAuth/delegated tokens: only the person's own sign-in manages their passkeys.

patch.description: Sets the name shown in the caller's passkey list (1-100 characters). Scoped to the signed-in person's own passkeys: anyone else's id is 404. 403 `person_credential_required` for API keys, portal links, agent and OAuth/delegated tokens: only the person's own sign-in manages their passkeys.

post.description: Starts the WebAuthn registration ceremony for the authenticated account: returns creation options plus an opaque handle that MUST be echoed back unchanged to finishPasskeyRegistration — it is how the server matches the attestation to this specific challenge. 409 webauthn_not_configured if the tenant has no relying party set up; 503 passkeys_disabled if ceremonies are turned off tenant-wide. 403 `person_credential_required` for API keys, portal links, agent and OAuth/delegated tokens: only the person's own sign-in manages their passkeys.

Completes the ceremony started by beginPasskeyRegistration: verifies the attestation response against the handle issued there and stores the credential under friendly_name. A stale, reused, or mismatched handle fails with the same 400 passkey_failed as a malformed attestation — the ceremony does not distinguish client bugs from a forged response in its error body. 403 `person_credential_required` for API keys, portal links, agent and OAuth/delegated tokens: only the person's own sign-in manages their passkeys.

Starts a passkey-only signup: a new person joins an OPEN workspace with nothing but a passkey (no email, no phone). Returns WebAuthn creation options (a discoverable, user-verifying passkey whose user handle is the new person's id) and an opaque `handle` to echo to finishPasskeySignup. Requires a passing Cloudflare Turnstile `turnstile_token`. Refusals: 403 `registration_rejected` (workspace not open-join, or inactive), 403 `wrong_auth_scheme` (a Privy-backed workspace), 409 `webauthn_not_configured` (no passkey relying party for this host), 403 `passkey_signup_unavailable` (off on this instance, Turnstile not configured, or the workspace's sign-in settings disallow passkeys), 403 `turnstile_failed`, 503 `turnstile_unavailable` (retry), 429 `passkey_signup_limit_reached` (the workspace's daily passkey-signup cap), 400 `invalid_display_name`, 404 `tenant_not_found` / `tenant_code_expired`. `GET /auth/config` reports `passkey_signup` for the workspace. Invites stay email-bound: an invite-only workspace cannot be joined this way.

requestBody.description: workspace, optional display name, Turnstile token

post.description: Completes a passkey-only signup: verifies the attestation against the `handle` from beginPasskeySignup, then in one transaction creates the person (no email, no phone), their `user` account in the workspace, a `passkey` identity link and the passkey, and signs them in (the session's `amr` is `["passkey"]`). The new person can sign in and join other open workspaces, but creating a workspace or sending invites answers 403 `verified_email_required` until they verify an email. Refusals: 400 `passkey_failed` (stale, reused or foreign handle; bad attestation, origin or relying party; no user verification; a passkey already registered), plus begin's workspace refusals, re-checked here (`registration_rejected`, `wrong_auth_scheme`, `passkey_signup_unavailable`, 429 `passkey_signup_limit_reached`).

Exchanges a `refresh_token` for a new access/refresh token pair. 401 `invalid_refresh_token` if the token is unknown or was already reused (reuse of a rotated-out token revokes the whole family — a theft signal), 409 `refresh_raced` when a concurrent refresh in the same family already rotated it (benign — retry with the client's latest stored token, do not treat as a logout).

Creates an account/person via the same per-provider verification `login` uses (see `login`'s description for the `provider` field rules), but returns the created account (`handler.RegisterResponse`) rather than issuing tokens; the caller must still call `login` (or, for `privy_custom_auth` tenants, complete the Privy flow) to sign in. 200 if the account already existed for this credential (idempotent), 201 if newly created, 409 `email_taken` if the email is already registered in this tenant under a different provider. An expired workspace code gets 404 `tenant_code_expired`.

get.description: The caller's own active and recent login sessions (device, IP, issued/last-seen times). Scoped to the caller only — there is no cross-account session listing here.

delete.description: Revoke one of the caller's own login sessions by its session/family id. A session not owned by the caller returns 404, never a cross-account 403 — this is not an existence oracle for other users' sessions.

post.description: Public: issues a single-use nonce for `wallet_address` (optionally scoped by `tenant_code`) that the client embeds in its EIP-4361 "Sign-In with Ethereum" message; `login` with `provider: siwe` then verifies `message`+`signature` against it. An expired workspace code gets 404 `tenant_code_expired`.

post.description: Public: starts a Twilio Verify SMS login challenge to `phone`, scoped by `tenant_code`. Always 200 `{message:"code sent"}` once the request is accepted; no SMS is sent for a number the tenant would refuse at login (invite-only workspace, unknown number). 400 if SMS verification isn't configured for the tenant (no Verify client wired or no active Twilio connection). An expired workspace code gets 404 `tenant_code_expired`. Send the Cloudflare Turnstile widget response as `turnstile_token`: when the deployment has Turnstile configured, a sent token that fails is 403 `turnstile_failed` (503 `turnstile_unavailable` if Cloudflare cannot be reached), and a deployment with `otp_require_turnstile` on refuses a missing one the same way. 429 `rate_limited` when the caller's address or the number's send budget (per number, across workspaces: by default 5 codes per 10 minutes and 20 per hour) is spent.

RelayState.description: relay state from the authn request

redirect to the tenant app with ?sso_code (or ?sso_error)
redirect to the tenant's identity provider

post.description: Starts a passkey approval of one action by the signed-in caller (today only `deposit`, with `amount` in cents and the client's deposit `nonce`). The options allow only the caller's Privy passkeys that are enrolled for MFA and carry a public key; 409 `no_passkey` when there is none. The relying party is the requesting page's origin, which must be one of the tenant webauthn connection's `stepup_origins`.

Verifies the passkey assertion for a handle from POST /auth/stepup/begin (single use: the handle is spent whether or not it verifies) and returns a step-up token: an RS256 JWT signed with the access-token key (same JWKS), typ `stepup`, aud `enforcer-cybrid`, amr `["passkey"]`, act/amt/nonce as begun, valid 120 s. It is not an access token and is refused as one. 401 `stepup_rejected` when the assertion does not approve.

Creates a membership for the caller's existing person in the tenant identified by `tenant_code` (an open/joinable tenant's invite code), reusing the same person rather than creating a new one. Idempotent if the caller already has an account there. Returns a fresh token pair scoped to that tenant. 201 if the membership was newly created, 200 if it already existed, 403 join-not-allowed and inactive-tenant cases, 404 if the code matches no tenant. An expired workspace code gets 404 `tenant_code_expired`.

Issues a new token pair scoped to the caller's account in a DIFFERENT tenant they already belong to, given that tenant's `tenant_id`. Requires the person's own sign-in (403 `person_session_required` for API keys, portal links, agents and token-exchange tokens). An OAuth access token from an authorization-code grant is also accepted and answered with an OAuth-shaped pair (`data.access_token`, `refresh_token`, `expires_in`, `scope`, `token_type`) for the target account that keeps the grant's client and audience and never widens its scope (clipped to the client's current ceiling); it refreshes at /oauth/token by that client. The target account must already have authorized that client (403 `consent_required`), and the result is audited as `auth.oauth_workspace_switched`. 403 `no_membership` if the caller's person has no account in the target tenant — this does not create one (see `joinTenant` for that). Exception: a platform admin (cross_tenant role) on an interactive session (not an API key, OAuth or token-exchange token) who has no account in the target gets one created with their current role, whatever the workspace's join policy; the response then has `is_new_account: true` and the entry is audited as `auth.tenant_joined` with `platform_admin_entry`.

get.description: Every tenant membership (account row) belonging to the caller's PERSON, across all tenants that person has an account in — the multi-tenant membership list `/auth/tenant/switch` picks from.

post.description: Public: confirms a Cloudflare Turnstile widget response token server-side (forwarding the caller's IP as `remoteip`) and reports pass/fail. A failed challenge is returned as 200 `{success:false, ...error codes}`, not a 4xx, so the client can distinguish "try the widget again" from a malformed request; 503 if no Turnstile secret is configured on this deployment (fails loud rather than silently passing every caller).

Evaluates an authorization decision for the caller (or, with `user_id`, for another account the caller may read).

**The `resource` is a description, not a lookup.** Nothing loads the row behind `resource.id`, so the request must carry whatever the rules match on — `owner_id` for the owner baseline, `tenant_id` for any tenant-scoped grant (including every admin-managed type: tenant, connection, email_template, terms, group_type, …). A request naming only `{type, id}` is judged against an empty tenant and an empty owner: it returns `allow:false` with `reason:"resource_unspecified"`, which means the request under-described the resource — not that a tenancy check failed.

Example of a same-tenant read that can actually be allowed:
`{"action":"read","resource":{"type":"account","id":"<id>","tenant_id":"<caller tenant>","owner_id":"<id>"}}`

**Leaf types** (`graph`, `graph_node`, `graph_run`, `graph_skill` — decided by the leaf service that owns them, ADR 0005): v3 cannot know the leaf's own answer (e.g. graph membership), so the check composes your tenant's and your account's deny rules over an ASSUMED leaf allow and returns `baseline:"assumed"`. `allow:true` then means "no policy of yours would refuse this"; whether the leaf allows it is the leaf's question (for graphs, `GET /graphs/{id}/access`).

get.description: Filter-scoped by role: a platform admin sees their own tenant's connections by default (tenant_id for another tenant, all_tenants=true for every tenant), tenant_admin sees their own tenant's, user/developer see none. List rows never carry config — only Get/Create/Update return a (redacted) config, and even those never return raw credentials. Filters only narrow that scope; total counts the rows matching every filter. q never searches config. Unknown provider/status values match nothing; an unknown sort falls back to created.

parameters.description: case-insensitive substring of the connection name or public provider_app_id (never config)

parameters.name: provider
parameters.description: csv of provider names (OR), e.g. sendgrid,privy — see GET /connections/providers

parameters.name: sort_dir
parameters.description: sort direction (id breaks ties in the same direction)

parameters.name: tenant_id
parameters.description: list this tenant instead of your own (default: the caller's own tenant, platform admins included). Another tenant requires the cross_tenant grant — 403 otherwise

parameters.name: all_tenants
parameters.description: list EVERY tenant (platform-wide admin view). Requires the cross_tenant grant — 403 otherwise. Mutually exclusive with tenant_id (400 conflicting_tenant_scope)

403.description: forbidden: tenant_id/all_tenants beyond your own tenant without the cross_tenant grant

post.description: Creates a connection in the CALLER's tenant (tenant_admin/admin only), or — for a platform admin whose role carries the cross_tenant grant — in the tenant named by the optional `tenant_id`. `tenant_id` omitted or equal to the caller's own tenant behaves exactly as before. A caller WITHOUT cross_tenant naming any other tenant gets 403 (never silently written to their own tenant); an unknown or deleted target tenant is 404; a target that already has a connection for this provider is 409 (update that one instead). config is sealed with AES-256-GCM before it touches the database and is never returned in plaintext by this or any other route — Create's response has the same redaction as Get. provider_id must resolve to a known provider (400 otherwise). A tenant-shaped body key other than `tenant_id` (e.g. `tenantId`) is a 400 unknown_param rather than being ignored. The audit event records both the caller's and the target tenant.

get.description: The global catalog of connection capability types (e.g. webhook receiver, third-party integration). Not tenant-scoped — every authenticated caller sees the same fixed list, independent of what their tenant has configured.

One connection with config REDACTED: only keys on an explicit per-provider public-key allowlist are returned in the clear (e.g. non-secret settings); every other key comes back as a fixed redacted-value marker, never the real credential. ResourceAuth-gated (tenant_admin/admin only) — the fenced value round-trips through PATCH without ever exposing the real secret.

delete.description: Removes the connection row (and its sealed credentials) permanently. Irreversible; a tenant relying on it (e.g. its only cdp/alchemy/quicknode webhook receiver, or a trello/rain integration) loses that capability immediately.

patch.description: Partial update (ResourceAuth write: tenant_admin/admin only). Scoped by the ROW's tenant, not the caller's: a platform admin (cross_tenant role) may update a connection in any tenant by id, a tenant_admin only in their own; there is no tenant_id field here and the row never moves tenant. A config field sent as the redacted marker value (i.e. round-tripping what Get returned) leaves that key's stored secret untouched rather than overwriting it with the literal marker — only fields with a REAL new value replace the sealed credential.

get.description: The caller's own address book. contact_type is linked (points at a real platform account) or custom (off-platform, owner-entered details). favorite=true returns only favorited contacts; favorites always sort first regardless of the sort param. Rows are overlaid (best-effort) with each linked contact's unacked-fulfillment badge from enforcer-cybrid — a badge omission means the overlay call failed or is disabled, not that the count is zero.

parameters.name: favorite
parameters.description: when true, only favorited contacts (favorite_rank set)

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: name / display_name (A-Z, default) | name_desc / display_name_desc | recent | oldest. Favorites always sort first; id breaks ties; an unknown value falls back to name.

post.description: Creates either a LINKED contact (pass contact_account_id — must be a discoverable account per the same rules as suggestions/lookup, or 403/404) or a CUSTOM one (omit it; requires at least one of name/email/phone/wallet — 400 bad_request otherwise). Duplicate detection is per-field: a repeat contact_account_id, custom_email, or custom_wallet_address returns 409 rather than a second row — scanning the same payment QR twice is expected to resolve to the existing contact. custom_wallet_address must be a validly-shaped address (400 invalid_wallet_address otherwise) and becomes the contact's pay-to destination.

post.description: Bulk-creates LINKED contacts from a list of account ids (ids in the body). Never fails as a batch: the response reports imported, skipped (already a contact — not an error), and failed (with a per-id reason in errors), so a caller can retry only the failures.

The caller's KNOWN on-chain destinations, derived from their own address

Returns an empty page (not an error) when the tenant has discovery turned off tenant-wide.

post.description:
Creates a payment intent — a "send" (sender defaults to the caller) or, when sender_user_id or sender_wallet names someone else, a "request" the caller becomes the receiver of. deadline is required RFC3339. memo is the join key to on-chain settlement: 409 memo_taken if it's already held by a live (pending/claimed/submitted) fulfillment in the tenant — omit it and the server mints one. 422 amount_over_limit if a DIRECT-tagged payment exceeds the per-payment cap (max_uoa/max_cents echoed in the error body).

**idempotency_key (optional, 8..255 chars) — pass one if your client can retry.** A second create with the same key in the same tenant returns the ORIGINAL fulfillment, same id, instead of minting a second payment. The key is durable for the row's whole life, so a retry that arrives after the original settled still resolves to it — that is the "response was lost, client retried" case. Without a key, behaviour is unchanged: every call creates a new payment intent. Note the counterparty notification fires only on the real create, never on a replay.

**reference tags reserved to services.** A reference starting `RWD:`, `REFUND:` or `DEPOSIT:` (case-insensitive, after trimming whitespace) is refused with 400 `reserved_reference`: those kinds are raised only by trusted services (POST /service/fulfillments, refunds, the deposit bridge). `BP:`, `DIRECT:`, `WD:` and `TERMINAL:` are accepted.

409.description: memo_taken — the supplied memo is already in use by a live (pending/claimed/submitted) fulfillment in this tenant. memo is the join key to on-chain settlement; omit it and the server mints one.

422.description: amount_over_limit — a DIRECT-tagged payment over the per-payment cap (max_uoa + max_cents in payload)

Global types are included in every scope. q matches name or description. total counts the rows matching q; an unknown sort falls back to the default order.

They are omitted without include=stats, and also when that aggregate fails (the page itself still returns). Groups of a RESERVED type (a service's, e.g. enforcer-graph's per-DAG sharing groups) are omitted unless include_reserved=true or type_id names that type. Archived groups are omitted unless archived=true|all.

get.description: One group by id (ResourceAuth read — baseline: any tenant member may read any group in their tenant). 404 group_not_found if it doesn't exist; no separate 403 for cross-tenant since the baseline rule already scopes visibility.

delete.description: Deletes a group (ResourceAuth write: the group's creator, its tenant's admin, or a system admin). A SOFT delete: the row is tombstoned and stops granting, but is no longer readable through the API — to retire a team while keeping the record that it existed and who was in it, use POST /groups/{id}/archive instead. 403 group_type_reserved on a group of a RESERVED type: only its service retires one.

patch.description: Updates a group's name/description/type (ResourceAuth write: creator, tenant admin, or system admin). 400 invalid_group_type if type_id doesn't resolve to a type the caller's tenant can use. 403 group_type_reserved on a group of a RESERVED type, or a retag onto one — those belong to their service. 409 group_archived on an archived group (unarchive first).

post.description: Retires a group WITHOUT deleting it: the group and its memberships are kept and stay readable (GET /groups/{id}, its members, its audit trail), but it leaves GET /groups unless archived=true|all, refuses edits and membership changes (409 group_archived), and STOPS GRANTING — its members' tokens no longer carry it, exactly as for a deleted group. Agents owned by the group are suspended, as on delete; unarchiving does not resume them. Idempotent: archiving an archived group returns it unchanged. Same gate as delete (ResourceAuth write: creator, tenant admin, system admin); 403 group_type_reserved on a group of a RESERVED type. Writes a group.archived audit record.

get.description: Invites whose group_ids contain this group. Visibility is GET /tenants/{id}/invites's: callers with tenant authority may pass all=true for every invite, everyone else sees only the invites they sent.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: filter by status: pending | accepted | expired | cancelled

post.description: Invite an email or wallet address into the group's tenant and, on acceptance, into this group. Same rules as POST /tenants/{id}/invites with group_ids=[id]: provide exactly one of email or wallet_address; callers without tenant authority always invite at the "user" role (another role returns 403). Gated like POST /groups/{id}/members: 403 if the caller may not add members to the group, 404 for a missing, retired or other-tenant group. 403 `verified_email_required` when the caller signed up with only a passkey and has not verified an email yet.

get.description: Members of a group, each as its account view plus the MEMBERSHIP: `membership.role` (member | manager), `membership.joined_at` and `membership.added_by` (null for system grants and memberships older than the field). role filters by membership role (400 invalid_role on any other value); joined_from/joined_to bound joined_at (YYYY-MM-DD = whole UTC day, or RFC3339; 400 on malformed); sort is name (default) | name_desc | joined | joined_desc, ties broken by account id. Peer contact fields are redacted unless the caller holds an admin-read grant.

parameters.name: q

parameters.description: joined before (YYYY-MM-DD = through that whole day, or RFC3339)

parameters.description: order; unknown values fall back to name

post.description: Adds one account to a group by account_id (ResourceAuth write on the group), optionally in a role (member, the default, or manager); an existing member keeps their role and joined_at — PATCH the membership to change the role. 400 invalid_role on any other role. 403 cross_tenant_member if the target account is not in the group's tenant — group membership never spans tenants. 403 group_type_reserved on a group of a RESERVED type unless the caller holds the tenant_manage grant. 409 group_archived on an archived group.

Adds many accounts to one group in a single call, reporting EVERY id's outcome rather than aborting on the first problem: `added`, `already_member` (membership is a set, so re-running an import is a no-op, not an error), `not_found`, or `cross_tenant`. Authorization is the same ResourceAuth write on the GROUP that the single-member POST runs — there is no per-account permission to add somebody to a group you may already write — so the ids in the body are data, not resources. A cross-tenant account is a row outcome here rather than the whole-request 403 the single-member path answers, because one bad line must not discard a correct import; the invariant is unchanged and such an account is never added. Duplicate ids within one call collapse, and the second mention reports already_member. One membership event and one audit record are written per member actually added, exactly as the single-member path writes them. role (member | manager, default member) applies to every ADDED member; existing members keep theirs; any other role is 400 invalid_role. 409 group_archived on an archived group. At most 1000 ids per call.

Removes many accounts from one group in a single call, reporting every id as `removed` or `not_member`. The verdict comes from the delete itself rather than a read beforehand, so two operators undoing the same bad import cannot both be told they removed someone. A POST rather than a DELETE because it carries a body. Same ResourceAuth write on the group as every other membership change, and one membership event plus one audit record per member actually removed — removal hard-deletes the row, so that audit record is the only durable trace the person was ever in the group. At most 1000 ids per call.

Moves accounts from this group to `to_group_id` in ONE transaction, so nobody is ever in neither group (reorganising teams no longer needs a remove and an add per person). The route authorizes a write on THIS group; the target is checked separately with the same write decision, so the caller must be able to add members to both (403 target_forbidden otherwise). The target must be a different, non-archived group in the same tenant (400 invalid_target). Every id reports an outcome: `moved`, `not_member` (not in this group), `not_found`, `cross_tenant`, or the agent fence's `agent_consent_required` / `not_group_member` for a service account entering the target. An account already in the target just leaves this group and reports `moved`. role sets the target role; omitted, each member keeps their role. Each mover gets a removed + added membership event and audit record pair (metadata.via = move). 409 group_archived if either group is archived. At most 1000 ids per call.

delete.description: Removes one account from a group by account_id. 404 membership_not_found if the pair doesn't exist as a membership — this endpoint does not distinguish "no such group" from "not a member".

patch.description: Changes one membership's role in place (member | manager). joined_at and added_by are kept, and ONE group.member_role_changed audit record (metadata: account_id, from, to) is written — where remove + re-add reset joined_at and wrote two. Setting the role a member already has is a no-op success with no audit row. The role is descriptive today: no authorization rule reads it. Same ResourceAuth write on the group as every membership change. 400 invalid_role, 404 membership_not_found, 403 group_type_reserved, 409 group_archived.

post.description: Restores an archived group: it lists, accepts edits and membership changes, and grants again, with the memberships it had when archived. Agents suspended by the archive stay suspended. Idempotent on a live group. Same gate as archive. Writes a group.unarchived audit record.

get.description: Reports the db plus every configured peer (mb, kv), each as a bare "ok"/"error" keyed by role — never by implementation. Wire dashboards/alerting here, NOT the readiness probe (use /health/ready, so a peer blip can't 503 auth). Public (no auth). Any failing check yields "degraded" with a 503.

503.description: degraded — one or more checks failing

get.description: Gates traffic on the hard dependency only (db). Peer services (mb, kv) are deliberately excluded — a downstream blip must not 503 the whole API; they remain visible on GET /health. Public (no auth). Returns "degraded" with a 503 when the db is unreachable.
Agents the caller owns or stewards.

Per-counterparty unacked sent + received tallies over live fulfillments (contact-dot source). Pass the SAME created_after the bell summary + drill-down list use (e.g. the 48h window) or contacts show ghost dots for ancient unseen rows the user can't see anywhere. Omit for lifetime counts.

parameters.description: pay-yourself fulfillments (sender == receiver): include keeps them (default), exclude hides them (match the bell/list filter or contacts show ghost dots), only returns just them

parameters.description: pending|confirmed|... or `outstanding` (= pending+claimed+submitted) or `closed` (= cancelled+declined+expired, the Declined tab)

Mark the caller's read-receipt (type=seen, default) or the receiver paid attestation (type=paid) on EVERY live fulfillment matching the filter — no id list, no page cap — so "mark all seen" clears badges beyond the loaded page. Filter axes (direction / contact / created_after window / self_payments) mirror the per-contact unseen-count badge, so the ack clears exactly what the badge counts. Idempotent; returns the number newly acknowledged.

get.description: Dashboard totals split by role (as_sender / as_receiver), each with outstanding + completed buckets and unseen counts.

A caller who is not a party to the fulfillment (or requests type=paid as the sender) gets 404, not 403. Idempotent set/clear, not a toggle.

Payer refuses an incoming payment request. Caller must be the fulfillment's sender_user_id (403 otherwise) and the row must still be status=pending — once it has moved to submitted, paid, or any terminal state this returns 409 not_pending rather than acting. On success the row moves to declined.

409.description: not_pending — already submitted/paid, no longer declinable; reward_not_declinable — a payout raised by a service (RWD:, payee is creator), which that service will pay regardless

post.description: Creates (idempotently, one per payer: per fulfillment and refund_address) a deposit intent and returns its CREATE2 forwarder address. Caller must be the fulfillment's payer or creator. refund_address is required and committed into the forwarder address. Notional above 10,000 USDC is refused. Pay Base only, MPP only, the exact amount_to_send, before expiry.

get.description: The fulfillment's creator, sender or payee only; anyone else gets 404 (existence is not revealed). Every deposit intent raised on it, oldest first, with state, received_amount, expires_at, forwarder_address and every transfer seen at the forwarder (receipts: tx hash, amount, block). Refund addresses are masked (`0x0fe0…8296`). Read-only.
get.summary: List a fulfillment's MPP deposit intents (its parties)

post.description: Creator withdraws (cancels) a fulfillment they created, while it is still pending or claimed. Caller must be created_by_user_id (403 otherwise).

409.description: reward_not_recallable — a payout raised by a service (RWD:, payee is creator), which that service will pay regardless

post.description: Records that the payer has broadcast the on-chain payment, moving the intent pending→submitted so it drops out of the payable set immediately. Idempotent: acking a payment that has ALREADY landed (the settlement webhook routinely confirms the row before this call arrives) returns 200 with the current record, not an error. 409 is reserved for a row that moved on for another reason — a different payer claimed it, or it expired/declined/cancelled/failed.

patch.description: Partial update of the caller's own person. A first_name or last_name in the patch is also copied onto the account display name teammates see in the directory and in group member lists: onto every one of the person's accounts when the person's own login session makes the edit, and onto the calling account alone for an API key, OAuth app or exchanged token, which act in one workspace. A non empty first_name or last_name must be at most 100 characters, contain a letter, and hold no control or invisible characters (400 invalid_name); an empty one clears it.

post.description: Gives the caller's own account a first name, only when it has none, so teammates in this workspace see a name instead of an email or nothing. This is what an AI app calls after asking the person what their team should call them. It writes only this account's display name: the person's own name, which identity checks read, and the person's accounts in other workspaces are never touched. It only fills: an account that already has a first name is 409 first_name_already_set and nothing is written, and changing a name is PATCH /me/person. A name is never replaced, even by a concurrent write. The name is trimmed and must be 1 to 100 characters, contain a letter, and hold no control or invisible characters (400 invalid_first_name). Tagged first-name so an OAuth client can be granted exactly this with the scope enforcer:first-name.write; a credential without it is 403 insufficient_scope.
post.summary: Set my first name when I have none

get.description: Every version your account has submitted, newest first, including refused ones and why.

post.description: Stores a new version of the rules your account puts on itself, and validates it. The policy must declare `package account.a_<your account id, dashes as underscores>` and may only DENY: it is evaluated after platform and tenant policy, only for requests your account makes, and a `deny` there refuses what they allowed. `allow` and `declared_types` are refused, because an account cannot grant itself anything. Otherwise it is validated exactly like a tenant policy — restricted builtins, the enforcer.v1 stdlib, the policy's own test_ rules — and a refused submission is stored with its reason and still returns 200, with the verdict in `validation`. Nothing changes until a version is activated.
post.summary: Submit a policy for your own account

get.description: Your account's active policy, or null when it has none — a 200 with null data, since having none is the ordinary state.

delete.description: Leaves your account with no policy of its own, answering to platform and tenant policy alone. Every version is kept.

get.description: The source as submitted, its status, and — when it was refused — the validation error.

post.description: Promotes a validated version of your account's policy and retires whatever was active. From then on its `deny` rules apply to every request your account makes, through every door — HTTP, gRPC, and POST /authz/check without a policy_id, which is how to see one work. Rolling back is activating an earlier version.
post.summary: Make one of your policy versions live

get.description: Every client registered at this authorization server, newest first. `include_disabled=true` also returns deregistered ones. Platform admin only.

delete.description: Disables a registered client: every subsequent /authorize and /token for this `client_id` fails as though it had never been registered. The row is retained for audit. Already-disabled and never-existed both answer 404. Does NOT revoke tokens the client already holds — those are ordinary enforcer tokens with their own expiry. Platform admin only.

patch.description: Replaces the client's allowed scopes with exactly the list given. Every scope must be one this deployment advertises in its metadata document (`scopes_supported`) or a fine scope of the form `enforcer:<tag>.<effect>` with effect `read`, `write` or `destructive`; an unknown scope answers 400 and names it. Existing consents and already-issued tokens are unaffected (their scope was fixed at issue): the new ceiling applies to the next /authorize consent and the next token exchange or refresh. A disabled or unknown client answers 404. Platform admin only.

Policies are whole Rego modules: there is no per-policy resource_type or effect to filter on.

post.description: Compiles and stores a new custom Rego policy under the fixed enforcer.custom package, live immediately with no restart — every replica compiles and caches it by content hash on first evaluation, not at deploy time. The module is UNTRUSTED CODE by construction: network/host builtins (http.send, net.lookup_ip_addr, opa.runtime) are stripped, so a policy referencing them fails to compile rather than being allowed to exfiltrate accessor data or reach the cluster network. A policy with no tenant_id (global, consumable by every tenant) requires the admin role — 403 forbidden otherwise for a tenant_admin caller.

get.description: One custom policy's stored Rego source and metadata. Readable per the same global-plus-own-tenant visibility as listPolicies.

put.description: Recompiles the stored Rego source in place, same untrusted-code constraints as createPolicy. Write access is role-gated, not ownership-gated: tenant_write for the policy's own tenant, cross_tenant (admin) for a global one — the row's creator (created_by) is provenance only and grants no standing write access, unlike the normal "write your own row" baseline, because a policy is executable authorization logic other tenants may consume.

delete.description: Deletes a compiled custom Rego policy from the live authorization engine. Any subsequent POST /authz/check that still names this policy_id falls through to the built-in static policy (policy.rego) rather than erroring — a deleted policy silently stops narrowing/widening decisions rather than breaking the check endpoint.

get.description: The published legal document of one type, readable WITHOUT authentication — it exists so a signed-out visitor (Stripe's Billing Portal requires a privacy-policy and terms-of-service URL an unauthenticated customer can open) reaches the same document the app shows. type is restricted to platform, privacy and cookies; every other value, including a valid-but-internal type such as aml or custom and any unknown string, answers 404 legal_document_not_published with the same body as a type that simply has nothing published — this route never confirms that a non-publishable document exists. Pass tenant=<uuid> to prefer that tenant's own version, which falls back to the platform-wide document when the tenant has none (scope tells you which answered); omit it for the platform-wide document. An unknown tenant id is indistinguishable from "not published". Only currently-effective documents are served: inactive, not-yet-effective and expired versions are 404. The body carries the document text and provenance only — no acceptance, account or mandatory-gate data. Cacheable for 5 minutes.

parameters.name: tenant
parameters.description: tenant uuid — prefer this tenant's version, falling back to the platform document

parameters.description: filter: true = KYC-verified only, false = not-yet-verified only

get.summary: Look up a public referral share link

get.description: The static role catalog (built-in + custom), open to ANY authenticated caller with no admin gate — this is the "populate a role picker" read, distinct from adminListRoles (GET /admin/roles) which serves the same rows behind the tenant_read admin gate for role administration. Small and unpaginated: total is the full row count and limit/offset describe the single page returned.

parameters.description: substring match over slug and name

parameters.description: filter by whether an agent is bound

The mint fence applies: the role may never exceed the caller's own Permissions (403 role_exceeds_caller), and a portal-link or agent credential may never mint one (403 agent_cannot_mint). slug is tenant-unique, case-insensitive (409 slug_taken otherwise) and immutable after creation.

get.description: One service account by id. 404 service_account_not_found for an unknown id, a human account's id, or a service account outside the caller's visibility — never distinguished, so the route is not an existence oracle.

delete.description: Soft-deletes a service account. Refused with 409 has_agent while an agent is bound — delete the agent instead.

patch.description: Changes name and/or description. slug and role are not editable here — role has its own fenced route (PUT .../role), and slug is immutable after creation.

put.description: Flips the active flag. false stops every credential of this service account on its next use — active is read fresh at credential-resolution time, never cached into a long-lived claim.

post.description: Mints an env3_ key OWNED BY the service account, created_by the caller. The plaintext appears in this response only. scope is capped at the caller's own credential scope (403 insufficient_scope otherwise), same ceiling rule POST /api-keys applies to a self-minted key.

delete.description: Hard-removes the key row. Unlike Revoke this leaves no row for audit; prefer the revoke route when the goal is to disable the credential while keeping a record it existed.

post.description: Deactivates the key (kept for audit). For a hard removal use DELETE on the same path.

Mints a replacement key carrying the outgoing key's name/scope/expiry, and pulls the outgoing key's own expiry in to now+grace_seconds (0..86400, default 0) instead of revoking it outright — a grace of 0 stops it on its very next use. The replacement's scope is capped at the caller's own credential scope exactly as POST .../api-keys caps a new key: an unscoped outgoing key comes back at the caller's ceiling, and one scoped wider than the caller is refused (403 insufficient_scope).

get.description: This service account's own audit trail — every event whose actor_account_id is this id.

post.description:
Service-key only (today enforcer-mp-merchant). Raises a refund of the settled payment `id`: an OPEN request the account that was paid settles from the wallet that received the sale, sent to the wallet that actually paid it.

**The body names an amount and nothing else.** Destination (`receiver_wallet` = the original's `payer_address`), payer (`sender_user_id` = the original's `receiver_user_id`), the wallet allowed to settle it (`expected_payer_wallet` = the original's `receiver_wallet`), token and chain are all read from the original. A caller that names the wrong payment refunds money to the person who paid THAT payment.

Refuses more than is refundable: what actually arrived (routed settlements) minus refunds already live or confirmed against it, checked under a lock on the original so two refunds cannot each claim the full balance. The refusal carries `refundable_uoa`.

Service-key only (today enforcer-airdrop). Records that the service broadcast the payout for reward fulfillment `id` from its treasury wallet: `pending` → `submitted` with `tx_hash`, then a best-effort settlement attempt from that transaction's receipt (the enforcer-reconcile sweep retries it regardless).

**Reward rows only.** The row must belong to `X-Tenant-ID` (404 otherwise — existence is not revealed across tenants) and its reference must carry the `RWD:` tag (403 `not_a_reward_fulfillment`); a service key cannot stamp a P2P, bill-pay or POS row.

**Idempotent.** A row that already carries this same hash — `submitted`, or `confirmed` because the Routed webhook got there first — answers 200 with the current row. A confirmed row with no hash is stamped with this one. A different hash is 409 `tx_hash_conflict`; an expired/declined/cancelled/failed row is 409 `not_pending`.

Settlement: a route-rail payout confirms from its `Routed(memo)` event as today. A send-rail payout (plain ERC-20 `transfer`) confirms from the Transfer log in this transaction whose token is `request_token`, recipient `receiver_wallet` and value at least `notional_uoa`.

post.description: Provisions a new tenant. An operator provisioning a workspace FOR a customer names the customer — to own it themselves they pass their own person id. The owner's plan allowance is deliberately NOT enforced on this path: an operator grant may legitimately exceed a plan (a comp, a pilot), and the excess is then visible as `owned` above `workspace_slots` on `getSelfServeTenantAllowance` rather than hidden as an unowned workspace.

The workspace's sign-in settings: what it has stored (null = inherit), the effective values its sign-ins use, where each came from (workspace, instance or default), and the range each may be set to. Audited with before and after values.

post.description: Makes the caller's person the OWNER of this workspace (`tenants.owner_person_id`), consuming one slot of their workspace plan — the counterpart of `selfServeTenant` for a workspace that already exists. Requires the caller to be a **tenant_admin of this workspace**: 403 `not_a_workspace_admin` otherwise, including for a platform admin who is not a member and for any portal credential. Only an UNOWNED workspace can be claimed — 409 `workspace_already_owned` if it has an owner, because moving ownership between people is a transfer and needs the current owner's authority, not the claimant's. 403 `workspace_limit_reached`, with the same counts and meaning as on `selfServeTenant`, when the caller already owns their plan's allowance (enforced only where `selfServeTenant` is enforced). Returns the caller's allowance AFTER the claim, the same shape `getSelfServeTenantAllowance` returns.

Replaces the tenant's join code with a freshly generated one and returns it in the response body (the only time the new value is shown in full). The OLD code stops working immediately for anyone trying to join with it: every join link and any invite text that embeds the old code goes stale, so this is a "the help-desk is about to get join-code tickets" action, not a routine rotation. The body is optional; when present it must be `application/json` with only `expires_at` (RFC 3339, in the future), or the call is a 400 and the code is not rotated. `expires_at` makes the new code stop resolving at that time everywhere a code is accepted, exactly as if it had been rotated away: new joins AND sign-in by code. Existing members who name the workspace by its code (the OAuth sign-in page, or any auth route given `tenant_code`) cannot sign in that way until an admin rotates again; SSO, Privy app sign-in and existing sessions are unaffected. Those routes answer 404 `tenant_code_expired`. Omitted, the code never expires. Each rotation sets the expiry afresh, and rotating is the only way to change it.

Internal staff notes are visible to staff only. from/to bound created_at (since/until are accepted aliases, so an incremental poll sends since=<last created_at>): YYYY-MM-DD is an inclusive whole UTC day, RFC3339 an exact instant (from inclusive, to exclusive); malformed is 400 invalid_from / invalid_to. total counts the messages matching the window.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: created_at lower bound (inclusive): YYYY-MM-DD or RFC3339

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: created_at upper bound: YYYY-MM-DD (inclusive day) or RFC3339 (exclusive)

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: alias of from (from wins when both are sent)

parameters.name: sort_dir
parameters.description: sort direction (id breaks ties in the same direction)

post.description: Append a message. internal=true is staff-only. Public replies drive the lifecycle: a requester reply reopens, a staff reply marks the ticket pending, and each notifies the other side.

429.description: challenge_in_progress — same-type async challenge initiated within the last 10s; honour Retry-After

get.description: The caller's person-level verifications (KYC packets, attestations), cross-tenant by construction because they hang off the person, not the account. Self-scoped: a filter narrows this set and can never reach another person's rows. With NO query string the response is the legacy `{success, data:[...], count}` shape, every row, submitted_at DESC — unchanged. With `limit` or `offset` the response is the ADR 0003 envelope `{success, data:{items, total, filtered, limit, offset}}`; `limit=0` returns counts alone. Filters or a sort WITHOUT `limit`/`offset` return the legacy shape over the filtered, sorted rows. `status`/`kind`/`issuer` are comma-separated ORs; an unrecognised member matches nothing. `q` is a case-insensitive substring over id, issuer and decision_reason — the row only; the person is not searched because the list is already one person's. `from`/`to` bound the column named by `date_field` (default submitted_at): `YYYY-MM-DD` is an inclusive whole UTC day, RFC3339 an exact instant (`to` exclusive); a row with no value in that column is excluded when a bound is set and included otherwise. `since`/`until` and `created_after`/`created_before` are aliases. Nullable sort columns (decided, expires) order NULLS LAST in both directions; every sort tiebreaks on id. An unknown query KEY is `400 unknown_param`.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: csv of statuses, OR'd (pending, approved, rejected, withdrawn, expired); unknown members match nothing

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: csv of kinds, OR'd (free-form column: identity, kyc, ...)

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: case-insensitive substring over id, issuer, decision_reason

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: date_field >= this (YYYY-MM-DD = start of that UTC day, or RFC3339)

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: date_field < this (YYYY-MM-DD = end of that UTC day inclusive, or RFC3339 exclusive)

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: page size 1..200 (clamped); 0 = counts only; absent = unpaged legacy shape

parameters.name: group_id
parameters.description: only when the caller's account is a member of this group (uuid); an empty list otherwise. 404 group_not_found if the group is not visible to you

parameters.name: exclude_group_id
parameters.description: only when the caller's account is NOT a member of this group (uuid); same 404 rule

400.description: unknown_param | invalid_limit | invalid_offset | invalid_from | invalid_to | invalid_window | invalid_group_id | invalid_exclude_group_id

get.description: The caller's own verification sessions (one row per provider and type). Self-scoped: a filter narrows this set and can never reach another account's rows. With NO query string the response is the legacy `{success, data:[...], count}` shape, every row, provider ASC — unchanged for existing clients. With `limit` or `offset` the response is the ADR 0003 envelope `{success, data:{items, total, filtered, limit, offset}}`: `total` is the caller's row count before filters, `filtered` after, `items` one page; `limit=0` returns the counts alone. Filters or a sort WITHOUT `limit`/`offset` return the legacy shape over the filtered, sorted rows. `status`/`type`/`provider` are comma-separated ORs; an unrecognised member matches nothing (never a 400). `q` is a case-insensitive substring match over session_id, provider, status and last_error. `from`/`to` bound "last moved" = verified_at, else updated_at: `YYYY-MM-DD` is an inclusive whole UTC day, RFC3339 an exact instant (`to` exclusive); malformed is a 400. `since`/`until` and `created_after`/`created_before` are accepted as aliases. Every sort tiebreaks on id in the same direction, so pages never repeat or skip a row. An unknown query KEY is `400 unknown_param`.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: csv of statuses, OR'd (pending, active, verified, failed, expired, revoked); unknown members match nothing

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: csv of verification types, OR'd (kyc, kyb, tax_id_selfie, ...)

parameters.name: provider
parameters.description: csv of provider slugs, OR'd (cybrid, activecampaign, ...)

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: case-insensitive substring over session_id, provider, status, last_error

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: last-moved >= this (YYYY-MM-DD = start of that UTC day, or RFC3339)

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: last-moved < this (YYYY-MM-DD = end of that UTC day inclusive, or RFC3339 exclusive)

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: page size 1..200 (clamped); 0 = counts only; absent = unpaged legacy shape

parameters.name: group_id
parameters.description: only when the caller's account is a member of this group (uuid); an empty list otherwise. 404 group_not_found if the group is not visible to you

parameters.name: exclude_group_id
parameters.description: only when the caller's account is NOT a member of this group (uuid); same 404 rule

400.description: unknown_param | invalid_limit | invalid_offset | invalid_from | invalid_to | invalid_window | invalid_group_id | invalid_exclude_group_id
